headline: Chip stocks lead a Black Friday rally, capping Wall Street's best week in more than a year
paragraphs: Oil had a choppy, thinly traded session on Friday. Prices rose in Asian hours after a reported Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, which added to worries after this week's strike on Ras Tanura, but much of that rise faded by the close. Brent's January contract ended at about US$95.40, up roughly 0.9% from Wednesday and about 3% on the week, its first weekly gain this month. WTI slipped to around US$83. Attention now turns to Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, where the group is expected to keep January quotas unchanged.

US stocks rallied in a shortened post-Thanksgiving session as chipmakers bounced back. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose nearly 5% and Micron gained more than 7% as worries over AI profitability eased. The Nasdaq jumped 2.3%, the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297 and the Dow added 1.2% to 50,775. All three gained more than 5% over the week, which AP called the market's best week in more than a year.
